    Data¶

    Load the hub data, build forecast vintages and simulate outbreaks to test models on. See Getting started for a worked example.

    bdbvhubrenewal.data ¶

    The data: hub data, vintages, synthetic vintages and external estimates.

    • tidy: download the hub's data streams and tidy and load them.
    • dates: epi weeks, reference dates and submission windows.
    • releases: release cut-offs and the publication lag of the renewal models.
    • simulate: simulated outbreaks published as vintages.
    • delays: empirical onset-to-report delays.
    • snapshots: daily release snapshots as arrays on the onset clock.
    • bvd: BVDOutbreakSize releases as of a forecast's cut-off.
    • zones: the hub's health-zone codes and weekly zone counts.

    The names of tidy are re-exported here.

    bdbvhubrenewal.data.tidy ¶

    Download, tidy and load the BDBV Modeling Hub data.

    The hub publishes these streams (see DATA_STREAMS):

    • target-data/time-series.csv: weekly confirmed cases by onset week, for the country, provinces and health zones, one block per as_of vintage. This is the target, observed plus imputed onsets.
    • auxiliary-data/daily-confirmed-case.csv: daily confirmed cases by onset day, split into observed and imputed onsets, per vintage.
    • auxiliary-data/weekly-reporting-delays-by-province.csv: one row per case with a known onset, giving its province, onset week and onset-to-report delay. Only the latest vintage is in the file. Earlier vintages are in archived-delay-data/ or only in the git history, so fetch_hub_data walks the history to find them all.
    • auxiliary-data/locations.csv and health-zone-code-mapping.csv: location codes, names and parents.
    • hub-config/: the round configuration, used for validation.

    The hub publishes no deaths, suspected cases, report-date series or populations. Province populations come from a cited public source instead (PROVINCE_POPULATIONS).

    The tidy tables written by build_tidy_data are small and committed under data/. Raw downloads go to data/raw/ and are not committed.

    HUB_REPO module-attribute ¶

    HUB_REPO: Final = 'InsightNet-US/BDBV-Modeling-Hub'

    The hub's GitHub repository.

    TARGET module-attribute ¶

    TARGET: Final = 'wk inc confirmed cases'

    The hub target this repository forecasts.

    DATA_STREAMS: Final[dict[str, str]] = {
    "target-data/time-series.csv": "Weekly confirmed cases by onset week and vintage (observed plus imputed onsets), for the country, provinces and health zones.",

    "auxiliary-data/weekly-reporting-delays-by-province.csv": "One row per known-onset case: province, onset week and onset-to-report delay in days. Latest vintage only; earlier vintages are in the archive folder or the git history.",
    "auxiliary-data/locations.csv": "Location codes, names, types and parents.",
    "auxiliary-data/health-zone-code-mapping.csv": "Health zone codes mapped to P-codes and DHIS2 codes.",
    "hub-config/tasks.json": "Round, task and output type configuration.",
    "hub-config/admin.json": "Hub settings, including the time zone.",
    "hub-config/model-metadata-schema.json": "Model metadata schema.",
}

    def write_csv(frame: pd.DataFrame, path: Path | str) -> None:
    """Write a table as CSV, gzipped when `path` ends in `.gz`.

    The bytes depend on the table only, so an unchanged table leaves its
    file, its git diff and any hash of it unchanged.

    Parameters
    ----------
    frame : pandas.DataFrame
        The table, written without its index.
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        Where to write it.
    """
    gz = Path(path).suffix == ".gz"
    frame.to_csv(path, index=False, compression=_GZIP if gz else None)

    def load_province_centres() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load the population-weighted centres of all 26 provinces.

    The mean of health zone centroids weighted by WorldPop 2025 counts,
    with zone boundaries from the Ministry of Health shapefile on the
    Humanitarian Data Exchange, via INRB-UMIE/BDBV2026-Data
    (`build/drc_health_zones.geojson` at `f7d3907`, CC BY 4.0).
    This is the source and method of epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize. The
    file ships with the package, so it does not depend on the data
    directory.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `worldpop` and
        `zones`.
    """
    path = files("bdbvhubrenewal.data").joinpath("province_centres.csv")
    with path.open() as fh:
        return pd.read_csv(fh, comment="#")

    def fetch_hub_data(
    raw_dir: Path | str,
    ref: str = "main",
    token: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Download the hub's data, including every vintage of the delay data.

    The latest versions of the files in `DATA_STREAMS` are taken from
    `ref`.
    For the delay data, every commit that touched `auxiliary-data/` is
    searched for delay files, and one file is kept per `as_of` vintage
    (from the most recent commit that has it).

    Parameters
    ----------
    raw_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        Where to save the files. Delay files go to `raw_dir/delays/`.
    ref : str
        Git ref of the hub to take the latest files from.
    token : str, optional
        GitHub token for the API. Defaults to `GITHUB_TOKEN` if set.
        Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 an hour, which is
        enough for one run.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A manifest with the commit SHA used and the source of each delay
        vintage. It is also written to `raw_dir/manifest.json`.
    """
    token = token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
    raw = Path(raw_dir)
    (raw / "delays").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    head = _api(f"repos/{HUB_REPO}/commits/{ref}", token)["sha"]
    for path in _LATEST_FILES:
        dest = raw / path
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest.write_bytes(_raw(head, path, token))

    commits = _api(
        f"repos/{HUB_REPO}/commits?path=auxiliary-data&sha={ref}&per_page=100",
        token,
    )
    delay_sources: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
    for commit in commits:  # newest first
        sha = commit["sha"]
        tree = _api(f"repos/{HUB_REPO}/git/trees/{sha}?recursive=1", token)
        paths = [
            item["path"]
            for item in tree["tree"]
            if item["path"].startswith("auxiliary-data/")
            and "reporting-delays" in item["path"]
            and item["path"].endswith(".csv")
        ]
        for path in paths:
            content = _raw(sha, path, token)
            as_of = _delay_as_of(content, path)
            if as_of in delay_sources:
                continue
            (raw / "delays" / f"{as_of}.csv").write_bytes(content)
            delay_sources[as_of] = {"commit": sha, "path": path}
    manifest = {
        "repo": HUB_REPO,
        "ref": ref,
        "commit": head,
        "downloaded": dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "delay_vintages": dict(sorted(delay_sources.items())),
    }
    (raw / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
    return manifest

    def tidy_locations(locations_csv: Path | str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy the country and province rows of `locations.csv`.

    Adds the 2019 population (`PROVINCE_POPULATIONS`, summed for the
    country) and the province centre where known.

    Parameters
    ----------
    locations_csv : pathlib.Path or str
        Path to the hub's `auxiliary-data/locations.csv`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `location_name`, `location_type`,
        `population`, `latitude` and `longitude`.
    """
    loc = pd.read_csv(locations_csv)
    loc = loc.loc[loc["location_type"].isin(["country", "province"])].copy()
    pop = pd.Series(PROVINCE_POPULATIONS, dtype="int64")
    loc["population"] = loc["location"].map(pop)
    loc.loc[loc["location"] == "CD", "population"] = int(pop.sum())
    loc["population"] = loc["population"].astype("int64")
    loc["latitude"] = loc["location"].map(
        {k: v[0] for k, v in PROVINCE_CENTRES.items()}
    )
    loc["longitude"] = loc["location"].map(
        {k: v[1] for k, v in PROVINCE_CENTRES.items()}
    )
    cols = [
        "location",
        "location_name",
        "location_type",
        "population",
        "latitude",
        "longitude",
    ]
    return loc[cols].reset_index(drop=True)

    def tidy_daily(daily_csv: Path | str, level: str = "province") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy daily onsets by vintage, for one level of geography.

    Parameters
    ----------
    daily_csv : pathlib.Path or str
        Path to the hub's `auxiliary-data/daily-confirmed-case.csv`.
    level : {"province", "zone"}
        The country and provinces, or the health zones, which are kept
        apart for a later zone stage.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `vintage`, `location`, `onset_date`, `observed` and
        `imputed`. Only days with at least one case are present.
    """
    types = {"province": ["country", "province"], "zone": ["health zone"]}
    if level not in types:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown level {level!r}: use {sorted(types)}.")
    raw = pd.read_csv(daily_csv)
    raw = raw.loc[raw["location_type"].isin(types[level])]
    raw = raw.assign(
        kind=np.where(raw["imputed"].astype(bool), "imputed", "observed")
    )
    wide = raw.pivot_table(
        index=["as_of", "location", "target_end_date"],
        columns="kind",
        values="observation",
        aggfunc="sum",
        fill_value=0,
    ).reset_index()
    for col in ("observed", "imputed"):
        if col not in wide.columns:
            wide[col] = 0
    wide = wide.rename(
        columns={"as_of": "vintage", "target_end_date": "onset_date"}
    )
    wide["vintage"] = wide["vintage"].map(release_id)
    wide.columns.name = None
    out = wide[["vintage", "location", "onset_date", "observed", "imputed"]]
    out = out.astype({"observed": "int64", "imputed": "int64"})
    return out.sort_values(["vintage", "location", "onset_date"]).reset_index(
        drop=True
    )

    def tidy_target(
    time_series_csv: Path | str, daily: pd.DataFrame
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy the target data for the country and provinces.

    Totals come from `time-series.csv`.
    The split into observed and imputed onsets comes from the daily file,
    summed into epi weeks.

    Parameters
    ----------
    time_series_csv : pathlib.Path or str
        Path to the hub's `target-data/time-series.csv`.
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `tidy_daily`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `kind` (always `"real"`), `vintage`, `location`,
        `location_name`, `target_end_date`, `observed`, `imputed` and
        `total`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If observed plus imputed does not equal the total in any row.
    """
    ts = pd.read_csv(time_series_csv)
    ts = ts.loc[
        (ts["target"] == TARGET)
        & ts["location_type"].isin(["country", "province"])
    ]
    ts = ts.rename(columns={"as_of": "vintage", "observation": "total"})
    ts["vintage"] = ts["vintage"].map(release_id)
    split = _weekly_split(daily)
    out = ts.merge(
        split, on=["vintage", "location", "target_end_date"], how="left"
    )
    out[["observed", "imputed"]] = (
        out[["observed", "imputed"]].fillna(0).astype("int64")
    )
    out["total"] = out["total"].astype("int64")
    bad = out["observed"] + out["imputed"] != out["total"]
    if bad.any():
        raise ValueError(
            f"{int(bad.sum())} rows where observed plus imputed is not "
            "the total."
        )
    out.insert(0, "kind", "real")
    cols = [
        "kind",
        "vintage",
        "location",
        "location_name",
        "target_end_date",
        "observed",
        "imputed",
        "total",
    ]
    return (
        out[cols]
        .sort_values(["vintage", "location", "target_end_date"])
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

        `target_end_date` and `total`. Zero rows are dropped.

    return (
        hz[cols]
        .sort_values(["vintage", "location", "target_end_date"])
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

    def tidy_delays(
    delay_files: Mapping[str, Path | str] | Path | str,
    locations: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy every vintage of the delay line data into one long table.

    Older files use a `location` column of short codes and newer files a
    `location_name` column, so both are mapped to hub location codes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delay_files : mapping of str to path, or a directory
        Vintage to file, or a directory of `<vintage>.csv` files as
        written by `fetch_hub_data`.
    locations : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `tidy_locations`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per known-onset case, with columns `vintage`,
        `location`, `location_name`, `onset_week` (the Saturday ending
        the onset week) and `delay` (days from onset to report).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a province name cannot be mapped to a location code.
    """
    if isinstance(delay_files, Path | str):
        files = {p.stem: p for p in sorted(Path(delay_files).glob("*.csv"))}
    else:
        files = {k: Path(v) for k, v in delay_files.items()}
    codes = _province_code_map(locations)
    names = dict(
        zip(locations["location"], locations["location_name"], strict=True)
    )
    frames = []
    for vintage, path in sorted(files.items()):
        df = pd.read_csv(path)
        key = "location_name" if "location_name" in df.columns else "location"
        loc = df[key].map(codes)
        if loc.isna().any():
            missing = sorted(set(df.loc[loc.isna(), key]))
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown provinces in {path}: {missing}")
        frames.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "vintage": release_id(vintage),
                    "location": loc,
                    "location_name": loc.map(names),
                    "onset_week": df["week_ending"].astype(str),
                    "delay": df["days_sym_to_report"].astype("int64"),
                }
            )
        )
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    return out.sort_values(
        ["vintage", "location", "onset_week", "delay"]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    def build_tidy_data(
    raw_dir: Path | str, out_dir: Path | str
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Tidy the raw downloads and write the tables to `out_dir`.

    Writes `locations.csv`, `target.csv`, `daily.csv`,
    `daily_zones.csv.gz`, `delays.csv.gz`, `health_zones.csv.gz` and
    `national-coherence.csv` (see `national_coherence`), and copies the
    hub configuration to `hub-config/` and the download manifest to
    `sources.json`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    raw_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        Directory written by `fetch_hub_data`.
    out_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        Directory for the tidy tables, usually `data/`.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to pandas.DataFrame
        The tidy tables, keyed by name.
    """
    raw, out = Path(raw_dir), Path(out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    locations = tidy_locations(raw / "auxiliary-data" / "locations.csv")
    daily_csv = raw / "auxiliary-data" / "daily-confirmed-case.csv"
    daily = tidy_daily(daily_csv)
    daily_zones = tidy_daily(daily_csv, level="zone")
    target = tidy_target(raw / "target-data" / "time-series.csv", daily)
    delays = tidy_delays(raw / "delays", locations)
    zones = tidy_health_zones(raw / "target-data" / "time-series.csv")
    tables = {
        "locations": locations,
        "target": target,
        "daily": daily,
        "daily_zones": daily_zones,
        "delays": delays,
        "health_zones": zones,
    }
    write_csv(locations, out / "locations.csv")
    write_csv(target, out / "target.csv")
    write_csv(daily, out / "daily.csv")
    write_csv(daily_zones, out / "daily_zones.csv.gz")
    write_csv(delays, out / "delays.csv.gz")
    write_csv(zones, out / "health_zones.csv.gz")
    write_csv(national_coherence(target), out / "national-coherence.csv")
    config = out / "hub-config"
    config.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for path in (raw / "hub-config").glob("*.json"):
        (config / path.name).write_text(path.read_text())
    manifest = raw / "manifest.json"
    if manifest.exists():
        (out / "sources.json").write_text(manifest.read_text())
    return tables

    def national_coherence(
    target: pd.DataFrame, national: str = "CD"
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compare the national counts with the sum of the provinces.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Tidy target table (`tidy_target` or `load_target`).
    national : str
        Location code of the country.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per kind, vintage, onset week and stream (`observed`,
        `imputed`, `total`), with the national count, the sum of the
        provinces and `gap` (national minus provinces). A week missing on
        one side counts as zero there.
    """
    keys = ["kind", "vintage", "target_end_date"]
    streams = list(COHERENCE_STREAMS)
    nat = (
        target.loc[target["location"] == national].groupby(keys)[streams].sum()
    )
    prov = (
        target.loc[target["location"] != national].groupby(keys)[streams].sum()
    )
    nat, prov = nat.align(prov, join="outer", fill_value=0)
    long = nat.reset_index().melt(
        id_vars=keys, var_name="stream", value_name="national"
    )
    long["provinces"] = (
        prov.reset_index()
        .melt(id_vars=keys, var_name="stream", value_name="provinces")[
            "provinces"
        ]
        .to_numpy()
    )
    long["gap"] = long["national"] - long["provinces"]
    return long.sort_values([*keys, "stream"]).reset_index(drop=True)

    def delays_for_vintage(
    delays: pd.DataFrame, vintage: str
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, str]:
    """Delay rows for a vintage, using the latest earlier one if it has none.

    The hub does not publish delays with every vintage (2026-08-18 has
    none) and can publish them late. Rather than fail, the latest delay
    vintage on or before `vintage` stands in, relabelled to `vintage`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delays : pandas.DataFrame
        Tidy delay rows with a `vintage` column.
    vintage : str
        The data vintage being forecast from.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of pandas.DataFrame and str
        The delay table with rows for `vintage`, and a note of what was
        used instead (empty when the vintage had its own delays).
    """
    if delays.empty or (delays["vintage"] == vintage).any():
        return delays, ""
    earlier = sorted(str(v) for v in delays["vintage"].unique() if v <= vintage)
    if not earlier:
        return delays, (
            f"delays: none published by {vintage}, so the model's default "
            "completeness lag was used"
        )
    use = earlier[-1]
    extra = delays.loc[delays["vintage"] == use].assign(vintage=vintage)
    note = (
        f"delays: none published for {vintage}, so used the {use} delays, "
        "the latest available"
    )
    return pd.concat([delays, extra], ignore_index=True), note

    def coherence_summary(
    target: pd.DataFrame, vintage: str, national: str = "CD"
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarise national coherence for one real vintage.

    This is the `coherence.json` record the submission CI reads (see
    `ci/INTEGRATION.md`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Tidy target table.
    vintage : str
        The real vintage to check.
    national : str
        Location code of the country.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `as_of`, `coherent`, per-stream summaries, the rows with a gap and
        how the models handle a gap.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the vintage has no real data.
    """
    rows = target.loc[
        (target["kind"] == "real") & (target["vintage"] == vintage)
    ]
    if rows.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"No real data for vintage {vintage}.")
    table = national_coherence(rows, national)
    gaps = table.loc[table["gap"] != 0]
    streams = {
        s: {
            "weeks_with_gap": int((g["gap"] != 0).sum()),
            "max_abs_gap": int(g["gap"].abs().max()) if len(g) else 0,
            "total_gap": int(g["gap"].sum()),
        }
        for s, g in table.groupby("stream")
    }
    return {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "as_of": vintage,
        "national": national,
        "coherent": gaps.empty,
        "streams": streams,
        "rows": [
            {
                "target_end_date": str(r["target_end_date"]),
                "stream": str(r["stream"]),
                "national": int(r["national"]),
                "provinces": int(r["provinces"]),
                "gap": int(r["gap"]),
            }
            for r in gaps.to_dict("records")
        ],
        "handling": COHERENCE_HANDLING,
    }

        A target table.

    def newly_missing(target: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return cases added between consecutive vintages, by onset status.

    For each location and each vintage after the first, the change in
    total observed and total imputed onsets since the previous vintage of
    the same kind.
    The imputed change approximates the number of cases without an onset
    reported between the two vintages.
    It is net of cases whose onset was filled in later, so it can be
    negative.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        A target table.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `kind`, `location`, `vintage`, `previous_vintage`,
        `days`, `new_observed`, `new_imputed`, `new_total` and
        `new_imputed_share`.
    """
    sums = target.groupby(["kind", "location", "vintage"], as_index=False)[
        ["observed", "imputed", "total"]
    ].sum()
    sums = sums.sort_values(["kind", "location", "vintage"])
    grp = sums.groupby(["kind", "location"])
    sums["previous_vintage"] = grp["vintage"].shift(1)
    for col in ("observed", "imputed", "total"):
        sums[f"new_{col}"] = sums[col] - grp[col].shift(1)
    out = sums.dropna(subset=["previous_vintage"]).copy()
    out["days"] = (
        pd.to_datetime(out["vintage"]) - pd.to_datetime(out["previous_vintage"])
    ).dt.days
    new_total = out["new_total"].where(out["new_total"] > 0)
    out["new_imputed_share"] = out["new_imputed"] / new_total
    cols = [
        "kind",
        "location",
        "vintage",
        "previous_vintage",
        "days",
        "new_observed",
        "new_imputed",
        "new_total",
        "new_imputed_share",
    ]
    out = out[cols].astype(
        {"new_observed": "int64", "new_imputed": "int64", "new_total": "int64"}
    )
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

    def revision_table(
    target: pd.DataFrame, reference_vintage: str | None = None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compare each vintage's counts with a later reference vintage.

    This is the reporting triangle in weekly form: how recent weeks fill
    in as later vintages arrive.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        A target table of one kind.
    reference_vintage : str, optional
        The vintage to compare against. Defaults to the latest.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `vintage`, `location`, `target_end_date`, `weeks_before`
        (whole weeks from the target week to the vintage's epi week),
        `total`, `reference_total` and `fraction` (`total` over
        `reference_total`, missing where the latter is zero).
    """
    ref = reference_vintage or max(target["vintage"])
    latest = target.loc[
        target["vintage"] == ref, ["location", "target_end_date", "total"]
    ].rename(columns={"total": "reference_total"})
    out = target.loc[
        target["vintage"] <= ref,
        ["vintage", "location", "target_end_date", "total"],
    ].merge(latest, on=["location", "target_end_date"], how="left")
    out["reference_total"] = out["reference_total"].fillna(0)
    vintage_week = pd.to_datetime(
        pd.Series([epiweek_end(v).isoformat() for v in out["vintage"]])
    )
    gap = vintage_week - pd.to_datetime(out["target_end_date"])
    out["weeks_before"] = (gap.dt.days // 7).to_numpy()
    out["fraction"] = out["total"] / out["reference_total"].where(
        out["reference_total"] > 0
    )
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

    def imputed_by_release(target: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:

        A target table.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `vintage`, `location`, `imputed`, `total` and
        `imputed_share`, summed over onset weeks, for places with cases.
    """
    out = target.groupby(["vintage", "location"], as_index=False)[
        ["imputed", "total"]
    ].sum()
    out = out.loc[out["total"] > 0].reset_index(drop=True)
    out["imputed_share"] = out["imputed"] / out["total"]
    return out

    def release_updates(counts: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return how each week's count changed between consecutive releases.

    Parameters
    ----------
    counts : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `vintage`, `location`, `target_end_date` and `total`.
        A place and week missing from a release has no cases in it, as in
        the health zone table.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        One row per release after the first, place and week of the earlier
        release that has cases in either, with `vintage` (the later
        release), `previous`, `location`, `target_end_date`,
        `weeks_before` (whole weeks from the week to the earlier release's
        epi week), `previous_total`, `total` and `change`.
    """
    keys = ["location", "target_end_date"]
    releases = sorted(counts["vintage"].unique())
    frames: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    for prev, vin in pairwise(releases):
        old = counts.loc[counts["vintage"] == prev, [*keys, "total"]]
        new = counts.loc[
            (counts["vintage"] == vin)
            & counts["target_end_date"].between(
                old["target_end_date"].min(), old["target_end_date"].max()
            ),
            [*keys, "total"],
        ]
        pair = old.merge(
            new, on=keys, how="outer", suffixes=("_previous", "")
        ).fillna({"total_previous": 0, "total": 0})
        pair = pair.loc[(pair["total_previous"] > 0) | (pair["total"] > 0)]
        frames.append(
            pair.rename(columns={"total_previous": "previous_total"}).assign(
                vintage=vin, previous=prev
            )
        )
    out = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    out[["previous_total", "total"]] = out[["previous_total", "total"]].astype(
        "int64"
    )
    out["change"] = out["total"] - out["previous_total"]
    release_week = pd.to_datetime(
        pd.Series([epiweek_end(v).isoformat() for v in out["previous"]])
    )
    gap = release_week - pd.to_datetime(out["target_end_date"])
    out["weeks_before"] = (gap.dt.days // 7).to_numpy()
    cols = [
        "vintage",
        "previous",
        *keys,
        "weeks_before",
        "previous_total",
        "total",
        "change",
    ]
    return out[cols]

    def downward_summary(updates: pd.DataFrame, by: Sequence[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Summarise how often and how much counts fell between releases.

    Parameters
    ----------
    updates : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `release_updates`.
    by : sequence of str
        Columns to summarise within, such as `("location",)`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The `by` columns with `weeks` (place-weeks compared), `fell`,
        `share_fell`, `cases_down` and `cases_up` (summed falls and rises),
        `downward_share` (`cases_down` over the summed absolute change)
        and `largest_fall`.
    """
    down = (-updates["change"]).clip(lower=0)
    up = updates["change"].clip(lower=0)
    frame = updates.assign(
        fell=updates["change"] < 0, cases_down=down, cases_up=up
    )
    out = frame.groupby(list(by)).agg(
        weeks=("change", "size"),
        fell=("fell", "sum"),
        cases_down=("cases_down", "sum"),
        cases_up=("cases_up", "sum"),
        largest_fall=("cases_down", "max"),
    )
    out["share_fell"] = out["fell"] / out["weeks"]
    moved = out["cases_down"] + out["cases_up"]
    out["downward_share"] = out["cases_down"] / moved.where(moved > 0)
    cols = [
        "weeks",
        "fell",
        "share_fell",
        "cases_down",
        "cases_up",
        "downward_share",
        "largest_fall",
    ]
    return out[cols].reset_index()

    bdbvhubrenewal.data.dates ¶

    Epi weeks, reference dates and submission windows.

    The hub uses epi weeks that run Sunday to Saturday. A week is labelled by its last day, a Saturday. A round is labelled by its reference_date, the Saturday ending the epi week in which a forecast is made. Submissions open on the Sunday and close at the end of the Tuesday of that week, in Kinshasa time (submissions_due from -6 to -4 days).

    HUB_TIMEZONE module-attribute ¶

    HUB_TIMEZONE = ZoneInfo('Africa/Kinshasa')

    The hub's time zone, from hub-config/admin.json.

    SUBMISSION_START_OFFSET module-attribute ¶

    SUBMISSION_START_OFFSET = -6

    First day of the submission window, relative to the reference date.

    SUBMISSION_END_OFFSET module-attribute ¶

    SUBMISSION_END_OFFSET = -4

    Last day of the submission window, relative to the reference date.

        The date. A `datetime.datetime` is reduced to its date.
    """
    if isinstance(value, dt.datetime):
        return value.date()
    if isinstance(value, dt.date):
        return value
    return dt.date.fromisoformat(value)

    ----------

        Any date.

    def weeks_between(start: dt.date | str, end: dt.date | str) -> int:
    """Count whole weeks from one Saturday to another.

    Parameters
    ----------
    start, end : datetime.date or str
        Saturdays.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        `(end - start) / 7`. Negative if `end` is before `start`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If either date is not a Saturday.
    """
    first, last = as_date(start), as_date(end)
    if not (is_saturday(first) and is_saturday(last)):
        raise ValueError("Both dates must be Saturdays.")
    return (last - first).days // 7

    def submission_window(
    reference_date: dt.date | str,
) -> tuple[dt.datetime, dt.datetime]:
    """Return the submission window of a round, in Kinshasa time.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reference_date : datetime.date or str
        The round's reference date, a Saturday.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of datetime.datetime
        The opening time (00:00 on the Sunday) and closing time (23:59:59
        on the Tuesday), both aware datetimes in `HUB_TIMEZONE`.
    """
    ref = as_date(reference_date)
    start_day = ref + dt.timedelta(days=SUBMISSION_START_OFFSET)
    end_day = ref + dt.timedelta(days=SUBMISSION_END_OFFSET)
    start = dt.datetime.combine(start_day, dt.time(0, 0), HUB_TIMEZONE)
    end = dt.datetime.combine(end_day, dt.time(23, 59, 59), HUB_TIMEZONE)
    return start, end

    def reference_date_for_vintage(vintage: dt.date | str) -> dt.date:
    """Return the first reference date a data vintage can be submitted to.

    This is the earliest Saturday whose submission window closes on or
    after the vintage date.
    A vintage released on a Saturday serves the round ending a week later.
    One released on a Friday also serves the round ending eight days later,
    because its own round's window closed on the Tuesday.

    Parameters
    ----------
    vintage : datetime.date or str
        The `as_of` date of the data.

    Returns
    -------
    datetime.date
        The reference date, a Saturday.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> reference_date_for_vintage("2026-10-24")
    datetime.date(2026, 10, 31)
    >>> reference_date_for_vintage("2026-08-18")
    datetime.date(2026, 8, 22)
    """
    day = as_date(vintage)
    ref = epiweek_end(day)
    while ref + dt.timedelta(days=SUBMISSION_END_OFFSET) < day:
        ref += dt.timedelta(days=7)
    return ref

    bdbvhubrenewal.data.releases ¶

    Release dates, cut-offs and the renewal model's report to publication lag.

    A hub release is labelled by its as_of date. From the 2026-11-01 release on, as_of is the extraction date, one day after the last reported case. Earlier releases were labelled one day early, by the last reported case (https://github.com/InsightNet-US/BDBV-Modeling-Hub/issues/90). release_id maps a label, as published or as the hub may rewrite it, to the label we key releases by, so results, the submission ledger and rounds keep their keys. extraction_date and last_report give a release's dates from either. cutoff_lags gives the days from a release to its data cut-off by weekday, for simulated releases. publication_lag_pmf estimates, from pairs of delay files, the lag from a case's report to its first publication, which the renewal models mix into their onset expectations.

    def release_id(as_of: dt.date | str) -> str:
    """Return the label we key a hub release by.

    A label in `ORIGINAL_AS_OF` is kept. If the hub rewrites one to its
    extraction date, a day later, it maps back. Other labels are kept.

    Parameters
    ----------
    as_of : datetime.date or str
        The release's `as_of`, as published or as rewritten.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The release's label, ISO formatted.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> release_id("2026-10-25"), release_id("2026-11-01")
    ('2026-10-24', '2026-11-01')
    """
    day = as_date(as_of)
    before = (day - dt.timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
    return before if before in ORIGINAL_AS_OF else day.isoformat()

    def extraction_date(as_of: dt.date | str) -> dt.date:

    ----------
    as_of : datetime.date or str

    last report is the day before its extraction.

    --------

    def cutoff_lags(daily: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[int, int]:
    """Days from release to data cut-off, by release weekday.

    The cut-off of a real release is its latest onset day. A weekday with
    no real release takes the median over the releases.

    Parameters
    ----------
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Real daily rows with `vintage` and `onset_date`
        (`bdbvhubrenewal.data.tidy_daily`).

    Returns
    -------
    dict of int to int
        Lag in days for every weekday, 0 (Monday) to 6.
    """
    last = pd.to_datetime(daily.groupby("vintage")["onset_date"].max())
    lag = (
        pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(last.index, index=last.index)) - last
    ).dt.days
    lag = lag.sort_index()
    weekday = pd.to_datetime(
        pd.Series(lag.index, index=lag.index)
    ).dt.day_of_week
    seen = lag.groupby(weekday).last()
    fill = int(np.median(lag.to_numpy()))
    return {w: int(seen.get(w, fill)) for w in range(7)}

    For each pair of consecutive delay vintages \(V_1 < V_2\) on or before as_of, the rows of \(V_2\) beyond those of \(V_1\) (by location, onset week and delay) were first published in \((V_1, V_2]\). A row with onset week \(W\) and delay \(d\) was reported on \(W - u + d\) for an onset \(u\) days before \(W\), so with \(u\) uniform on \(0..6\) and publication uniform over the days of \((V_1, V_2]\) its lag is spread over \(V_1 + j - (W - u + d)\), the feasible (non-negative) ones only, and lags past max_lag go to the last cell. Pairs whose later vintage is after as_of are not used, so a backtest does not see later files.

    def publication_lag_pmf(
    delays: pd.DataFrame,
    as_of: dt.date | str,
    max_lag: int = MAX_PUBLICATION_LAG,
) -> np.ndarray | None:
    r"""Empirical pmf of the lag from report to first publication.

    For each pair of consecutive delay vintages $V_1 < V_2$ on or before
    `as_of`, the rows of $V_2$ beyond those of $V_1$ (by location, onset
    week and delay) were first published in $(V_1, V_2]$. A row with
    onset week $W$ and delay $d$ was reported on $W - u + d$ for an onset
    $u$ days before $W$, so with $u$ uniform on $0..6$ and publication
    uniform over the days of $(V_1, V_2]$ its lag is spread over
    $V_1 + j - (W - u + d)$, the feasible (non-negative) ones only, and
    lags past `max_lag` go to the last cell. Pairs whose later vintage is after
    `as_of` are not used, so a backtest does not see later files.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delays : pandas.DataFrame
        Delay rows of several vintages, with a `vintage` column.
    as_of : datetime.date or str
        The forecast date.
    max_lag : int
        Last lag cell, in days.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray or None
        Pmf on `0..max_lag`, or None if no pair is available.
    """
    day = as_date(as_of).isoformat()
    vintages = sorted(str(v) for v in delays["vintage"].unique() if v <= day)
    key = ["location", "onset_week", "delay"]
    mass = np.zeros(max_lag + 1)
    for a, b in itertools.pairwise(vintages):
        before = delays.loc[delays["vintage"] == a].groupby(key).size()
        after = delays.loc[delays["vintage"] == b].groupby(key).size()
        change = after.sub(before, fill_value=0).clip(lower=0)
        added = change[change > 0].reset_index(name="n")
        if added.empty:
            continue
        v1, v2 = pd.Timestamp(a), pd.Timestamp(b)
        gap = (v2 - v1).days
        onset = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(added["onset_week"]))
        week = (onset - v1).dt.days.to_numpy()
        count = np.asarray(added["n"], dtype=float)
        delay = np.asarray(added["delay"], dtype=int)
        # Lag for publication day j in 1..gap and onset u days before W.
        lag = (
            np.arange(1, gap + 1)[None, :, None]
            - week[:, None, None]
            + np.arange(7)[None, None, :]
            - delay[:, None, None]
        )
        keep = lag >= 0
        # Each row's count is spread over its feasible lags.
        per_row = count / np.maximum(keep.sum(axis=(1, 2)), 1)
        weight = np.broadcast_to(per_row[:, None, None], lag.shape)
        mass += np.bincount(
            np.minimum(lag[keep], max_lag),
            weights=weight[keep],
            minlength=max_lag + 1,
        )
    if mass.sum() == 0:
        return None
    return mass / mass.sum()

    bdbvhubrenewal.data.simulate ¶

    Simulate province outbreaks and publish them as hub-style vintages.

    The simulator draws from the model's own components with known parameters, so recovery can be checked and there is one implementation of the maths. Expected daily infections come from the model's renewal (bdbvhubrenewal.model.renewal.coupled_renewal), with its generation interval, gravity kernel, importation and depletion of the effective population, for \(\log R_p(t) = \log R(t) + \delta_p\) with a national \(R(t)\) that turns and fixed province offsets \(\delta_p\). Expected onsets are infections convolved with the model's incubation period (bdbvhubrenewal.model.model.incubation_period). Confirmed cases are Poisson with mean \(\alpha(t)\) times expected onsets. Each is reported after a double censored Gamma delay (bdbvhubrenewal.model.censored.censored_pmf) whose mean \(\mu(t)\) changes over time, has no onset with probability \(\pi\) at its report day, and is published after a lag of 0 to 3 days.

    SimulatedOutbreak.vintage publishes what the hub would show at a date: known onsets by onset week, missing onsets given an onset by subtracting a delay drawn from the hub's imputation delay at that date (bdbvhubrenewal.data.delays.hub_delay_pmf), their total, and the delay line data. SimulatedOutbreak.truth is the final total once every case is reported.

    MAX_SIM_DELAY module-attribute ¶

    MAX_SIM_DELAY = 120

    Longest simulated onset-to-report delay in days.

    RELEASE_WEEKDAYS module-attribute ¶

    RELEASE_WEEKDAYS = (1, 2, 4, 5)

    Release weekdays (Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday), as the real releases fell.

    RT_CAP module-attribute ¶

    Largest Rt in a calibrated scenario; onsets beyond it are seeds.

    "flat": 1.0,
    "rising": 1.25,
}

    Rt after the data, as a multiple of each province's Rt over the last three weeks of the data period, for each calibrated scenario.

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
class SimulationSettings:
    r"""Known parameters of a simulated outbreak.

    Times are days from `start`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Scenario name.
    start : datetime.date
        Day 0, a Sunday.
    n_days : int
        Days simulated.
    locations : tuple of str
        Provinces.
    seed_day : tuple of int
        Day each province is seeded (-1 for importation only).
    seed_size : int
        Onsets seeded on the seed day.
    log_r_offset : tuple of float
        Province offsets $\delta_p$ on log R.
    r_start, r_end : float
        National R before and after the turn.
    turn_day : int
        Centre of the turn in R.
    turn_width : float
        Days over which R turns (logistic scale).
    importation : float
        Share $\varepsilon$ of transmission sent to other provinces.
    effective_fraction : float
        Effective population as a share of the resident population.
    ascertainment : tuple of float
        $\alpha$ at day 0 and at the end, changing logistically mid-way.
    missing : tuple of float
        $\pi$ at day 0, at its peak (day `n_days` / 3) and at the end,
        by report day as in the model.
    delay_mean : tuple of float
        Mean delay at day 0 and at the end, changing linearly.
    delay_cv : float
        Coefficient of variation of the delay.
    publication_lag : tuple of float
        Pmf of the days from report to publication in a vintage, from 0.
        The default is the model's `PRIOR_PUBLICATION_LAG`: 85% uniform
        on 0..3 days and 15% uniform on 4..60 days, a tail of late
        entries as in the real delay files.
    backfill_share : float
        Share of cases reported with no onset whose onset is recorded
        later.
    backfill_delay : tuple of int
        Range of days from publication to the onset being recorded.
    gi_mean, gi_sd : float
        Generation interval mean and SD in days.
    seed : int
        Random seed.
    rt_paths, seed_curves : tuple of tuple of float, optional
        Daily Rt and seed infections by province, `(P, n_days)`, in place of
        the turning-point Rt and single seeds (`calibrated_settings`).
    delay_pmfs : tuple of tuple of float, optional
        Delay pmf on 0..60 days by onset day, in place of the Gamma delay.
        Days past the last row take the last row.
    missing_path : tuple of float, optional
        $\pi$ by report day, in place of the piecewise linear share.
    removal_share : float
        Share of cases removed from the data later (downward revisions).
    removal_delay : tuple of int
        Range of days from publication to removal.
    zone_shares : tuple of tuple, optional
        `(province, zone, share)` rows: each case is placed in a zone of
        its province with these shares.
    """

    name: str = "turning_point"
    start: dt.date = dt.date(2026, 4, 5)
    n_days: int = 238
    locations: tuple[str, ...] = ("CD-IT", "CD-NK", "CD-HU", "CD-TO")
    seed_day: tuple[int, ...] = (0, 30, -1, -1)
    seed_size: int = 5
    log_r_offset: tuple[float, ...] = (0.05, 0.0, -0.05, -0.15)
    r_start: float = 1.6
    r_end: float = 0.85
    turn_day: int = 120
    turn_width: float = 7.0
    importation: float = 0.01
    effective_fraction: float = 0.005
    ascertainment: tuple[float, float] = (0.5, 0.75)
    missing: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.05, 0.25, 0.12)
    delay_mean: tuple[float, float] = (12.0, 6.0)
    delay_cv: float = 1.0
    publication_lag: tuple[float, ...] = PRIOR_PUBLICATION_LAG
    backfill_share: float = 0.3
    backfill_delay: tuple[int, int] = (7, 42)
    gi_mean: float = GI_MEAN
    gi_sd: float = GI_SD
    seed: int = 1
    rt_paths: tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...] | None = None
    seed_curves: tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...] | None = None
    delay_pmfs: tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...] | None = None
    missing_path: tuple[float, ...] | None = None
    removal_share: float = 0.0
    removal_delay: tuple[int, int] = (7, 42)

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
class SimulatedOutbreak:
    """A simulated outbreak: the true parameters and the case line list.

    Attributes
    ----------
    settings : SimulationSettings
        The settings used.
    parameters : pandas.DataFrame
        Daily true values by province: `date`, `location`, `rt`,
        `susceptible_fraction`, `onsets`, `ascertainment`, `missing` and
        `delay_mean`.
    cases : pandas.DataFrame
        One row per confirmed case: `location`, `onset_date`,
        `report_date`, `publish_date`, `onset_known` (recorded when first
        published) and `onset_known_date` (when the onset is recorded,
        NaT if never).
    """

    settings: SimulationSettings
    parameters: pd.DataFrame
    cases: pd.DataFrame = field(repr=False)

    def vintage(
        self,
        as_of: dt.date | str,
        rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
        cutoff_lag: int = 0,
    ) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
        """Publish the data the hub would show at a date.

        Parameters
        ----------
        as_of : datetime.date or str
            The vintage date.
        rng : numpy.random.Generator, optional
            For the back-sampling draws. Seeded from the date by default.
        cutoff_lag : int
            Days from the release to the data cut-off. The release holds
            what was published by the cut-off.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple of pandas.DataFrame
            The target rows (as `bdbvhubrenewal.data.tidy_target`, with
            `kind = "simulated"`) and the delay line data.
        """
        day = as_date(as_of)
        known, missing, imputed_onset = self._published(day, rng, cutoff_lag)
        delays = (known["report_date"] - known["onset_date"]).dt.days.to_numpy()

        def weekly(loc: pd.Series, onset: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
            week = onset.map(lambda x: epiweek_end(x.date()).isoformat())
            return pd.DataFrame({"location": loc, "week": week}).value_counts()

        obs = weekly(known["location"], known["onset_date"]).rename("observed")
        imp = weekly(missing["location"], imputed_onset).rename("imputed")
        weeks = pd.date_range(
            epiweek_end(self.settings.start), epiweek_end(day), freq="7D"
        ).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        index = pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
            [list(self.settings.locations), list(weeks)],
            names=["location", "week"],
        )
        tab = pd.concat([obs, imp], axis=1).reindex(index).fillna(0)
        tab = tab.astype("int64").reset_index()
        tab = tab.rename(columns={"week": "target_end_date"})
        nat = tab.groupby("target_end_date", as_index=False)[
            ["observed", "imputed"]
        ].sum()
        nat["location"] = NATIONAL
        tab = pd.concat([tab, nat], ignore_index=True)
        tab["total"] = tab["observed"] + tab["imputed"]
        tab["location_name"] = tab["location"]
        tab["kind"] = "simulated"
        tab["vintage"] = day.isoformat()
        cols = [
            "kind",
            "vintage",
            "location",
            "location_name",
            "target_end_date",
            "observed",
            "imputed",
            "total",
        ]
        delay_rows = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "vintage": day.isoformat(),
                "location": known["location"].to_numpy(),
                "location_name": known["location"].to_numpy(),
                "onset_week": [
                    epiweek_end(x.date()).isoformat()
                    for x in known["onset_date"]
                ],
                "delay": delays.astype("int64"),
            }
        )
        return tab[cols], delay_rows

    def _published(
        self,
        day: dt.date,
        rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
        cutoff_lag: int = 0,
    ) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
        """Cases in the data at `day`: known, missing and imputed onsets."""
        rng = rng or np.random.default_rng(
            [self.settings.seed, day.toordinal()]
        )
        cut = pd.Timestamp(day - dt.timedelta(days=cutoff_lag))
        cases = self.cases
        seen = cases.loc[
            (cases["publish_date"] <= cut) & ~(cases["removed_date"] <= cut)
        ]
        # A case counts as known once its onset is recorded, which for a
        # backfilled case is after it was first published.
        has_onset = seen["onset_known_date"] <= cut
        known = seen.loc[has_onset]
        missing = seen.loc[~has_onset]
        pmf = hub_delay_pmf(day)
        draws = rng.choice(pmf.size, size=len(missing), p=pmf)
        imputed_onset = missing["report_date"] - pd.to_timedelta(
            draws, unit="D"
        )
        return known, missing, imputed_onset

    def zone_vintage(
        self, as_of: dt.date | str, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Publish the health zone totals the hub would show at a date.

        Each case keeps its zone; missing onsets take the same imputed
        onset as in `vintage`, so zones add up to provinces.

        Parameters
        ----------
        as_of : datetime.date or str
            The vintage date.
        rng : numpy.random.Generator, optional
            As for `vintage`.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Rows as `bdbvhubrenewal.data.load_health_zones`: `vintage`,
            `location`, `location_name`, `province`, `target_end_date`,
            with `observed` (known onsets) and `imputed` beside `total`.
        """
        day = as_date(as_of)
        known, missing, imputed_onset = self._published(day, rng)
        onset = pd.concat([known["onset_date"], imputed_onset])
        both = pd.concat([known, missing])
        week = onset.map(lambda x: epiweek_end(x.date()).isoformat())
        cases = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "location": both["zone"].to_numpy(),
                "province": both["location"].to_numpy(),
                "target_end_date": week.to_numpy(),
                "observed": np.r_[
                    np.ones(len(known), int), np.zeros(len(missing), int)
                ],
            }
        )
        cases["imputed"] = 1 - cases["observed"]
        out = cases.groupby(
            ["location", "province", "target_end_date"], as_index=False
        )[["observed", "imputed"]].sum()
        out["total"] = out["observed"] + out["imputed"]
        out = out.loc[out["location"] != ""]
        out["location_name"] = out["location"]
        out["vintage"] = day.isoformat()
        cols = [
            "vintage",
            "location",
            "location_name",
            "province",
            "target_end_date",
            "observed",
            "imputed",
            "total",
        ]
        return out[cols].reset_index(drop=True)

    def daily_vintage(
        self,
        as_of: dt.date | str,
        rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
        cutoff_lag: int = 0,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Publish the daily release the hub would show at a date.

        The counts are those of `vintage` (same draws for the imputed
        onsets), split by onset day, so each week's daily counts add up to
        its weekly total.

        Parameters
        ----------
        as_of : datetime.date or str
            The release date.
        rng : numpy.random.Generator, optional
            As for `vintage`.
        cutoff_lag : int
            As for `vintage`.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `kind` (`"simulated"`), `vintage`, `location`,
            `onset_date`, `observed`, `imputed` and `cutoff` (the data
            cut-off, ISO format), with the country and provinces and only
            days with a case.
        """
        day = as_date(as_of)
        known, missing, imputed_onset = self._published(day, rng, cutoff_lag)

        def daily(loc: pd.Series, onset: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
            return pd.DataFrame(
                {"location": loc, "onset_date": onset.dt.normalize()}
            ).value_counts()

        obs = daily(known["location"], known["onset_date"]).rename("observed")
        imp = daily(missing["location"], imputed_onset).rename("imputed")
        prov = pd.concat([obs, imp], axis=1).fillna(0).astype("int64")
        prov = prov.reset_index()
        nat = prov.groupby("onset_date", as_index=False)[
            ["observed", "imputed"]
        ].sum()
        out = pd.concat([prov, nat.assign(location=NATIONAL)])
        out["onset_date"] = out["onset_date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        out["kind"] = "simulated"
        out["vintage"] = day.isoformat()
        out["cutoff"] = (day - dt.timedelta(days=cutoff_lag)).isoformat()
        cols = [
            "kind",
            "vintage",
            "location",
            "onset_date",
            "observed",
            "imputed",
            "cutoff",
        ]
        return (
            out[cols]
            .sort_values(["location", "onset_date"])
            .reset_index(drop=True)
        )

    def vintages(
        self,
        dates: list[dt.date] | list[str],
        cutoff_lags: Mapping[int, int] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
        """Publish several vintages and stack them.

        Parameters
        ----------
        dates : list of datetime.date or str
            Vintage dates.
        cutoff_lags : mapping of int to int, optional
            Days from release to data cut-off by release weekday
            (`bdbvhubrenewal.data.releases.cutoff_lags`). None for no
            cut-off.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple of pandas.DataFrame
            Stacked target rows and delay line data.
        """
        parts = [
            self.vintage(d, cutoff_lag=_cutoff(d, cutoff_lags)) for d in dates
        ]
        return (
            pd.concat([p[0] for p in parts], ignore_index=True),
            pd.concat([p[1] for p in parts], ignore_index=True),
        )

    def daily_vintages(
        self,
        dates: list[dt.date] | list[str],
        cutoff_lags: Mapping[int, int] | None = None,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Publish several daily releases and stack them.

        Parameters
        ----------
        dates : list of datetime.date or str
            Release dates, for example `release_dates`.
        cutoff_lags : mapping of int to int, optional
            As for `vintages`.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Daily rows (`daily_vintage`) for every date.
        """
        parts = [
            self.daily_vintage(d, cutoff_lag=_cutoff(d, cutoff_lags))
            for d in dates
        ]
        return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)

    def truth(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return the final weekly totals by onset week.

        The final total of a week is every confirmed case with onset in
        it, whether or not the onset was recorded. The hub's imputation
        moves missing onsets between weeks, so this is the target only
        approximately.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `truth`.
        """
        kept = self.cases.loc[self.cases["removed_date"].isna()]
        week = kept["onset_date"].map(
            lambda x: epiweek_end(x.date()).isoformat()
        )
        tab = (
            pd.DataFrame({"location": kept["location"], "week": week})
            .value_counts()
            .rename("truth")
            .reset_index()
            .rename(columns={"week": "target_end_date"})
        )
        nat = tab.groupby("target_end_date")["truth"].sum().reset_index()
        nat["location"] = NATIONAL
        out = pd.concat([tab, nat], ignore_index=True)
        return out[["location", "target_end_date", "truth"]]

    def zone_vintage(
    self, as_of: dt.date | str, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Publish the health zone totals the hub would show at a date.

    Each case keeps its zone; missing onsets take the same imputed
    onset as in `vintage`, so zones add up to provinces.

    Parameters
    ----------
    as_of : datetime.date or str
        The vintage date.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator, optional
        As for `vintage`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Rows as `bdbvhubrenewal.data.load_health_zones`: `vintage`,
        `location`, `location_name`, `province`, `target_end_date`,
        with `observed` (known onsets) and `imputed` beside `total`.
    """
    day = as_date(as_of)
    known, missing, imputed_onset = self._published(day, rng)
    onset = pd.concat([known["onset_date"], imputed_onset])
    both = pd.concat([known, missing])
    week = onset.map(lambda x: epiweek_end(x.date()).isoformat())
    cases = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "location": both["zone"].to_numpy(),
            "province": both["location"].to_numpy(),
            "target_end_date": week.to_numpy(),
            "observed": np.r_[
                np.ones(len(known), int), np.zeros(len(missing), int)
            ],
        }
    )
    cases["imputed"] = 1 - cases["observed"]
    out = cases.groupby(
        ["location", "province", "target_end_date"], as_index=False
    )[["observed", "imputed"]].sum()
    out["total"] = out["observed"] + out["imputed"]
    out = out.loc[out["location"] != ""]
    out["location_name"] = out["location"]
    out["vintage"] = day.isoformat()
    cols = [
        "vintage",
        "location",
        "location_name",
        "province",
        "target_end_date",
        "observed",
        "imputed",
        "total",
    ]
    return out[cols].reset_index(drop=True)

    def daily_vintage(
    self,
    as_of: dt.date | str,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
    cutoff_lag: int = 0,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Publish the daily release the hub would show at a date.

    The counts are those of `vintage` (same draws for the imputed
    onsets), split by onset day, so each week's daily counts add up to
    its weekly total.

    Parameters
    ----------
    as_of : datetime.date or str
        The release date.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator, optional
        As for `vintage`.
    cutoff_lag : int
        As for `vintage`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `kind` (`"simulated"`), `vintage`, `location`,
        `onset_date`, `observed`, `imputed` and `cutoff` (the data
        cut-off, ISO format), with the country and provinces and only
        days with a case.
    """
    day = as_date(as_of)
    known, missing, imputed_onset = self._published(day, rng, cutoff_lag)

    def daily(loc: pd.Series, onset: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            {"location": loc, "onset_date": onset.dt.normalize()}
        ).value_counts()

    obs = daily(known["location"], known["onset_date"]).rename("observed")
    imp = daily(missing["location"], imputed_onset).rename("imputed")
    prov = pd.concat([obs, imp], axis=1).fillna(0).astype("int64")
    prov = prov.reset_index()
    nat = prov.groupby("onset_date", as_index=False)[
        ["observed", "imputed"]
    ].sum()
    out = pd.concat([prov, nat.assign(location=NATIONAL)])
    out["onset_date"] = out["onset_date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    out["kind"] = "simulated"
    out["vintage"] = day.isoformat()
    out["cutoff"] = (day - dt.timedelta(days=cutoff_lag)).isoformat()
    cols = [
        "kind",
        "vintage",
        "location",
        "onset_date",
        "observed",
        "imputed",
        "cutoff",
    ]
    return (
        out[cols]
        .sort_values(["location", "onset_date"])
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

    def vintages(
    self,
    dates: list[dt.date] | list[str],
    cutoff_lags: Mapping[int, int] | None = None,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Publish several vintages and stack them.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dates : list of datetime.date or str
        Vintage dates.
    cutoff_lags : mapping of int to int, optional
        Days from release to data cut-off by release weekday
        (`bdbvhubrenewal.data.releases.cutoff_lags`). None for no
        cut-off.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of pandas.DataFrame
        Stacked target rows and delay line data.
    """
    parts = [
        self.vintage(d, cutoff_lag=_cutoff(d, cutoff_lags)) for d in dates
    ]
    return (
        pd.concat([p[0] for p in parts], ignore_index=True),
        pd.concat([p[1] for p in parts], ignore_index=True),
    )

    def daily_vintages(
    self,
    dates: list[dt.date] | list[str],
    cutoff_lags: Mapping[int, int] | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Publish several daily releases and stack them.

    ----------

    cutoff_lags : mapping of int to int, optional
        As for `vintages`.

    def truth(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the final weekly totals by onset week.

    The final total of a week is every confirmed case with onset in
    it, whether or not the onset was recorded. The hub's imputation
    moves missing onsets between weeks, so this is the target only
    approximately.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date` and `truth`.
    """
    kept = self.cases.loc[self.cases["removed_date"].isna()]
    week = kept["onset_date"].map(
        lambda x: epiweek_end(x.date()).isoformat()
    )
    tab = (
        pd.DataFrame({"location": kept["location"], "week": week})
        .value_counts()
        .rename("truth")
        .reset_index()
        .rename(columns={"week": "target_end_date"})
    )
    nat = tab.groupby("target_end_date")["truth"].sum().reset_index()
    nat["location"] = NATIONAL
    out = pd.concat([tab, nat], ignore_index=True)
    return out[["location", "target_end_date", "truth"]]

    def release_dates(first: dt.date | str, last: dt.date | str) -> list[str]:
    """List the release days from `first` to `last`.

    Releases fall on `RELEASE_WEEKDAYS`, as the real releases did.

    Parameters
    ----------
    first, last : datetime.date or str
        First and last day, inclusive.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        ISO dates of the release days.
    """
    days = pd.date_range(as_date(first), as_date(last), freq="D")
    return [
        d.date().isoformat() for d in days if d.weekday() in RELEASE_WEEKDAYS
    ]

    def simulate_outbreak(
    settings: SimulationSettings | None = None,
) -> SimulatedOutbreak:
    """Simulate an outbreak with known parameters.

    Parameters
    ----------
    settings : SimulationSettings, optional
        Defaults to the `turning_point` scenario.

    Returns
    -------
    SimulatedOutbreak
        The parameters and line list.
    """
    s = settings or SimulationSettings()
    rng = np.random.default_rng(s.seed)
    n_loc, n_days = len(s.locations), s.n_days
    t = np.arange(n_days, dtype=float)
    gi = generation_interval(s.gi_mean, s.gi_sd)
    turn = _logistic((t - s.turn_day) / s.turn_width)
    log_r = np.log(s.r_start) + turn * (np.log(s.r_end) - np.log(s.r_start))
    rt = np.exp(log_r[None, :] + np.array(s.log_r_offset)[:, None])
    # Expected onsets from the model's own renewal, per resident with
    # the effective share at risk as the pool, as in `build_model`.
    pop = np.array([PROVINCE_POPULATIONS[p] for p in s.locations], float)
    seeding = np.zeros((n_days, n_loc))
    for i, day in enumerate(s.seed_day):
        if day >= 0:
            seeding[day, i] = s.seed_size / pop[i]
    if s.rt_paths is not None and s.seed_curves is not None:
        rt = np.asarray(s.rt_paths, dtype=float)
        seeding = np.asarray(s.seed_curves, dtype=float).T / pop
    table = pd.DataFrame({"location": s.locations, "population": pop})
    mixing = mixing_matrix(
        jnp.asarray(model_gravity_kernel(s.locations, table)),
        s.importation,
        jnp.asarray(pop / pop.sum()),
    )
    nu = s.effective_fraction
    x, r_eff, _ = coupled_renewal(
        jnp.zeros((gi.size, n_loc)),
        jnp.asarray(rt.T),
        jnp.asarray(gi),
        mixing,
        pool=nu,
        seeding=jnp.asarray(seeding),
    )
    # Onsets follow infections after the incubation period, as in the model.
    eta = incubation_period()
    infections = np.asarray(x, float)
    onsets = (
        np.stack([np.convolve(col, eta)[:n_days] for col in infections.T])
        * pop[:, None]
    )
    # Share of the pool still susceptible: R_eff / R, 1 where R is 0.
    sus = np.divide(
        np.asarray(r_eff, float).T, rt, out=np.ones_like(rt), where=rt > 0
    )

    frac = _logistic((t - n_days / 2) / 14)
    asc = s.ascertainment[0] + frac * (s.ascertainment[1] - s.ascertainment[0])
    peak = n_days / 3
    pi0, pi_peak, pi_end = s.missing
    miss = np.where(
        t <= peak,
        pi0 + (pi_peak - pi0) * t / peak,
        pi_peak + (pi_end - pi_peak) * (t - peak) / (n_days - peak),
    )
    if s.missing_path is not None:
        path = np.asarray(s.missing_path, dtype=float)
        miss = path[np.minimum(np.arange(n_days), path.size - 1)]
    mu = s.delay_mean[0] + (s.delay_mean[1] - s.delay_mean[0]) * t / n_days
    # Daily double censored Gamma delays, as the model's `censored_pmf`,
    # long enough that truncation is negligible.
    delay_cdf = np.cumsum(
        np.asarray(
            jax.vmap(
                lambda m: censored_pmf("gamma", m, s.delay_cv, MAX_SIM_DELAY)
            )(jnp.asarray(mu))
        ),
        axis=1,
    )
    if s.delay_pmfs is not None:
        rows_pmf = np.asarray(s.delay_pmfs, dtype=float)
        rows_pmf = rows_pmf[np.minimum(np.arange(n_days), len(rows_pmf) - 1)]
        delay_cdf = np.cumsum(rows_pmf, axis=1)
        mu = rows_pmf @ np.arange(rows_pmf.shape[1])

    lag_pmf = np.asarray(s.publication_lag) / np.sum(s.publication_lag)
    rows = []
    for i, loc in enumerate(s.locations):
        confirmed = rng.poisson(asc * onsets[i])
        days = np.repeat(np.arange(n_days), confirmed)
        u = rng.uniform(size=days.size) * delay_cdf[days, -1]
        delay = (delay_cdf[days] < u[:, None]).sum(axis=1)
        report = days + delay
        report_day = np.minimum(report.astype(int), n_days - 1)
        known = rng.uniform(size=days.size) >= miss[report_day]
        lag = rng.choice(len(s.publication_lag), days.size, p=lag_pmf)
        publish = report.astype(int) + lag
        lo, hi = s.backfill_delay
        filled = ~known & (rng.uniform(size=days.size) < s.backfill_share)
        later = publish + rng.integers(lo, hi + 1, size=days.size)
        onset_known_day = np.where(
            known, publish, np.where(filled, later, -1)
        ).astype(float)
        onset_known_day[onset_known_day < 0] = np.nan
        removed_day = np.full(days.size, np.nan)
        # Draw only when removals are on, so the default outbreak keeps its
        # random stream.
        if s.removal_share > 0:
            removed = rng.uniform(size=days.size) < s.removal_share
            lo, hi = s.removal_delay
            gone = publish + rng.integers(lo, hi + 1, size=days.size)
            removed_day = np.where(removed, gone, np.nan)
        zone = np.full(days.size, "", dtype=object)
        mine = [(z, w) for p, z, w in s.zone_shares if p == loc]
        if mine:
            names, weights = zip(*mine, strict=True)
            share = np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
            zone = rng.choice(
                np.asarray(names), days.size, p=share / share.sum()
            )
        rows.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "location": loc,
                    "onset_day": days,
                    "report_day": report.astype(int),
                    "publish_day": publish,
                    "onset_known_day": onset_known_day,
                    "removed_day": removed_day,
                    "zone": zone,
                    "onset_known": known,
                }
            )
        )
    cases = pd.concat(rows, ignore_index=True)
    start = pd.Timestamp(s.start)
    cases["onset_date"] = start + pd.to_timedelta(cases["onset_day"], unit="D")
    cases["report_date"] = start + pd.to_timedelta(
        cases["report_day"], unit="D"
    )
    cases["publish_date"] = start + pd.to_timedelta(
        cases["publish_day"], unit="D"
    )
    cases["onset_known_date"] = start + pd.to_timedelta(
        cases["onset_known_day"], unit="D"
    )
    cases["removed_date"] = start + pd.to_timedelta(
        cases["removed_day"], unit="D"
    )
    cases = cases[
        [
            "location",
            "zone",
            "onset_date",
            "report_date",
            "publish_date",
            "onset_known",
            "onset_known_date",
            "removed_date",
        ]
    ]

    dates = pd.date_range(start, periods=n_days, freq="D")
    params = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "date": np.tile(dates, n_loc),
            "location": np.repeat(s.locations, n_days),
            "rt": rt.reshape(-1),
            "susceptible_fraction": sus.reshape(-1),
            "onsets": onsets.reshape(-1),
            "ascertainment": np.tile(asc, n_loc),
            "missing": np.tile(miss, n_loc),
            "delay_mean": np.tile(mu, n_loc),
        }
    )
    return SimulatedOutbreak(s, params, cases)

    calibrated_settings ¶

    calibrated_settings(
    target: DataFrame,
    delays: DataFrame,
    zones: DataFrame,
    as_of: str,
    name: str = "flat",
    weeks_after: int = 10,
    settled_weeks: int = 4,
    seed: int = 1,
) -> SimulationSettings

    Build a scenario calibrated to the real data of one vintage.

    Each province's expected infections follow its real weekly onset totals at as_of, spread over the days of each week, smoothed and moved earlier by the mean incubation period, up to settled_weeks before as_of (later weeks are still being reported). Rt is the ratio of infections to the force of infection under the model's generation interval, \(R_p(t) = \lambda_p(t) / \sum_s g(s) \lambda_p(t - s)\), capped at RT_CAP, and infections beyond what that explains (first cases and reintroductions) are seeds, so the model's renewal reproduces the real curve. After that Rt is the mean of its last three weeks times SCENARIO_RT_SCALE[name], for weeks_after weeks past as_of. Ascertainment is 1, importation and depletion are off, so confirmed onsets follow the real curve.

    The delay is the real delay by onset week (_weekly_delay_pmfs), the missing-onset share is the real imputed share by onset week moved later by the mean delay to date it by report day, and health zones take the real share of each province's cases by zone. Late entries and onset backfill keep the simulator's defaults, and 2% of cases are removed 7 to 42 days after publication, so totals can be revised down.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    target DataFrame

    Real target rows, delay rows and health zone rows.

    		 required
    delays DataFrame

    Real target rows, delay rows and health zone rows.

    		 required
    zones DataFrame

    Real target rows, delay rows and health zone rows.

    		 required
    as_of str

    The real vintage to calibrate to.

    		 required
    name ('falling', 'flat', 'rising')

    Rt after the data.

    		 "falling"
    weeks_after int

    Weeks simulated past as_of.

    		 10
    settled_weeks int

    Weeks before as_of treated as still being reported.

    		 4
    seed int

    The scenario, named calibrated_{name}.

    def calibrated_settings(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    delays: pd.DataFrame,
    zones: pd.DataFrame,
    as_of: str,
    name: str = "flat",
    weeks_after: int = 10,
    settled_weeks: int = 4,
    seed: int = 1,
) -> SimulationSettings:
    r"""Build a scenario calibrated to the real data of one vintage.

    Each province's expected infections follow its real weekly onset
    totals at `as_of`, spread over the days of each week, smoothed and
    moved earlier by the mean incubation period, up to `settled_weeks`
    before `as_of` (later weeks are still being reported). Rt is the
    ratio of infections to the force of infection under the model's
    generation interval, $R_p(t) = \lambda_p(t) /
    \sum_s g(s) \lambda_p(t - s)$, capped at `RT_CAP`, and infections
    beyond what that explains (first cases and reintroductions) are seeds,
    so the model's renewal reproduces the real curve. After that Rt is the
    mean of its last three weeks times `SCENARIO_RT_SCALE[name]`, for
    `weeks_after` weeks past `as_of`. Ascertainment is 1, importation and
    depletion are off, so confirmed onsets follow the real curve.

    The delay is the real delay by onset week (`_weekly_delay_pmfs`),
    the missing-onset share is the real imputed share by onset week moved
    later by the mean delay to date it by report day, and health zones
    take the real share of each province's cases by zone. Late entries
    and onset backfill keep the simulator's defaults, and 2% of cases are
    removed 7 to 42 days after publication, so totals can be revised
    down.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target, delays, zones : pandas.DataFrame
        Real target rows, delay rows and health zone rows.
    as_of : str
        The real vintage to calibrate to.
    name : {"falling", "flat", "rising"}
        Rt after the data.
    weeks_after : int
        Weeks simulated past `as_of`.
    settled_weeks : int
        Weeks before `as_of` treated as still being reported.
    seed : int
        Random seed.

    Returns
    -------
    SimulationSettings
        The scenario, named `calibrated_{name}`.
    """
    real = target.loc[
        (target["vintage"] == as_of)
        & (target["kind"] == "real")
        & (target["location"] != NATIONAL)
    ]
    wide = real.pivot_table(
        index="target_end_date",
        columns="location",
        values="total",
        aggfunc="sum",
    ).fillna(0)
    wide = wide.loc[:, wide.sum() > 0]
    first_week = pd.Timestamp(
        str(wide.index[int((wide.sum(axis=1) > 0).argmax())])
    )
    start = (first_week - pd.Timedelta(days=13)).date()
    end = pd.Timestamp(as_of)
    n_days = (end - pd.Timestamp(start)).days + 1 + 7 * weeks_after
    settled = end - pd.Timedelta(weeks=settled_weeks)
    n_data = (settled - pd.Timestamp(start)).days + 1
    locs = tuple(str(c) for c in wide.columns)
    g = generation_interval()
    lead = round(INCUBATION_MEAN)
    n_inf = n_data - lead
    rt_rows, seed_rows = [], []
    for loc in locs:
        daily = np.zeros(n_days)
        for week, total in zip(wide.index, wide[loc], strict=True):
            day0 = (pd.Timestamp(str(week)) - pd.Timestamp(start)).days - 6
            if day0 >= 0 and day0 + 7 <= n_data:
                daily[day0 : day0 + 7] = total / 7
        daily = np.convolve(daily, np.ones(7) / 7, mode="same")[:n_days]
        # Infections lead onsets by the mean incubation period.
        daily = np.r_[daily[lead:], np.zeros(lead)]
        seeds = np.zeros(n_days)
        rt = np.zeros(n_days)
        for t in range(n_inf):
            past = daily[max(0, t - g.size) : t][::-1]
            force = float(g[: past.size] @ past)
            # Rt up to RT_CAP carries the curve, and onsets beyond what
            # transmission explains (first cases, reintroductions) are
            # seeds, so the renewal gives back the real curve.
            rt[t] = min(daily[t] / force, RT_CAP) if force > 1e-6 else 0.0
            seeds[t] = max(daily[t] - rt[t] * force, 0.0)
        recent = rt[n_inf - 21 : n_inf]
        recent = recent[recent > 0]
        level = float(np.mean(recent)) if recent.size else 0.0
        rt[n_inf:] = level * SCENARIO_RT_SCALE[name]
        rt_rows.append(tuple(rt))
        seed_rows.append(tuple(seeds))

    weeks = [
        (first_week + pd.Timedelta(weeks=k)).date().isoformat()
        for k in range(-1, n_days // 7 + 1)
    ]
    pmfs = _weekly_delay_pmfs(
        delays.loc[delays["vintage"] == as_of], weeks, as_of
    )
    daily_pmfs = np.repeat(pmfs, 7, axis=0)[:n_days]
    mean_delay = round(float(pmfs[:-1].mean(axis=0) @ np.arange(61)))
    nat = real.groupby("target_end_date")[["imputed", "total"]].sum()
    share = (nat["imputed"] + 1) / (nat["total"] + 2)
    share = share.rolling(5, center=True, min_periods=1).mean()
    miss = np.full(n_days, float(share.iloc[-settled_weeks - 1]))
    for week, value in zip(share.index, share, strict=True):
        end_day = pd.Timestamp(str(week))
        day0 = (end_day - pd.Timestamp(start)).days - 6
        if 0 <= day0 < n_days and end_day <= settled:
            miss[day0 : day0 + 7] = value
    miss = np.r_[np.full(mean_delay, miss[0]), miss][:n_days]
    zone_rows = zones.loc[zones["vintage"] == as_of]
    zone_tot = zone_rows.groupby(["province", "location"], as_index=False)[
        "total"
    ].sum()
    zone_shares = tuple(
        (str(p), str(z), float(v))
        for p, z, v in zone_tot.itertuples(index=False)
        if p in locs and v > 0
    )
    return SimulationSettings(
        name=f"calibrated_{name}",
        start=start,
        n_days=n_days,
        locations=locs,
        seed_day=tuple(-1 for _ in locs),
        importation=0.0,
        effective_fraction=1.0,
        ascertainment=(1.0, 1.0),
        rt_paths=tuple(rt_rows),
        seed_curves=tuple(seed_rows),
        delay_pmfs=tuple(tuple(r) for r in daily_pmfs),
        missing_path=tuple(miss),
        removal_share=0.02,
        zone_shares=zone_shares,
        seed=seed,
    )

    bdbvhubrenewal.data.delays ¶

    Onset-to-report delay distributions.

    The interface is small. A DelayModel is fitted to the delay line data of one vintage and returns a DelayFit. A DelayFit gives a daily pmf for any province and onset week, so a model can use delays that vary by place and time.

    EmpiricalDelayModel takes the empirical pmf over a rolling window of onset weeks and shrinks each province towards the pooled pmf, so small provinces and recent weeks stay stable. It ignores right truncation and the weekly censoring of onset, so recent delays are biased short.

    The renewal models fit their own delay with the cases, as the Delays section of the Renewal models methods page describes.

    DEFAULT_MAX_DELAY module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_MAX_DELAY: Final = 60

    Longest delay kept, in days. Longer delays are dropped (about 0.3%).

    HUB_DOUBLE_CENSORED_FROM module-attribute ¶

    HUB_DOUBLE_CENSORED_FROM: Final = dt.date(2026, 11, 1)

    First release whose imputation delay fit is double interval censored.

    The hub changed its fit with the 2026-11-01 release and left the earlier releases unchanged, so they keep the exact fit.

    HUB_GENGAMMA module-attribute ¶

    HUB_GENGAMMA: Final = {
    "exact": (
        5.12406648030701,

}
